results.name: last_vs_first_example_digit
results.description: In multi-example sets whose first and last shown examples have different final digits, yes-rate for targets sharing the LAST example's final digit minus yes-rate for targets sharing the FIRST example's final digit; nonzero observed vs null means presentation order (recency/primacy) matters, which the order-blind model cannot produce (positive = recency).

results.name: prime_odd_targets_odd_sets
results.description: In sets whose examples are all odd but not all prime, among odd targets, yes-rate for prime targets minus non-prime odd targets; observed > null means people favour prime-looking targets beyond what the model (prime family only active when all examples are prime) produces.

results.name: outside_range_distance_corr
results.description: Among multi-example sets, for targets outside [min,max] of the examples, Pearson correlation of yes with distance to the nearest range bound; observed more negative than null means endorsement decays with distance beyond the range more gradually/strongly than the model's step-like bounds produce.

results.name: singleton_proximity_corr
results.description: Among single-example sets (target != example), Pearson correlation of yes with log(1+|target-example|); observed more negative than null means people use numeric proximity more than the model's one-sided magnitude bounds predict (model under-produces the distance gradient).
results.code:
# name: singleton_proximity_corr
# description: Among single-example sets (target != example), Pearson correlation of yes with log(1+|target-example|); observed more negative than null means people use numeric proximity more than the model's one-sided magnitude bounds predict (model under-produces the distance gradient).
def test_statistic(df):
    k = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.count(",") + 1
    sub = df[k == 1]
    x = sub["number_set"].astype(int).values
    t = sub["target"].astype(int).values
    keep = t != x
    d = np.log1p(np.abs(t - x)[keep].astype(float))
    r = sub["rating"].values[keep].astype(float)
    if len(r) < 3 or d.std() == 0 or r.std() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.corrcoef(d, r)[0, 1])

results.name: trial_index_drift
results.description: Pearson correlation between trial_index and yes response across all trials; nonzero observed vs a ~0 null means yes-rate drifts over the session (fatigue/criterion shift) which the stationary model does not produce (sign gives drift direction).

results.name: sharpness_singleton_vs_large
results.description: Std across targets of per-(set,target) yes-rates, averaged within single-example sets minus averaged within 3-4-example sets; observed > null means singleton generalization is more graded/sharp relative to large sets than the model's single slope across set sizes produces (i.e. model under-differentiates targets for singletons, or over-differentiates for large sets if lower).
results.code:
# name: sharpness_singleton_vs_large
# description: Std across targets of per-(set,target) yes-rates, averaged within single-example sets minus averaged within 3-4-example sets; observed > null means singleton generalization is more graded/sharp relative to large sets than the model's single slope across set sizes produces (i.e. model under-differentiates targets for singletons, or over-differentiates for large sets if lower).
def test_statistic(df):
    k = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.count(",") + 1
    cell = df.assign(k=k).groupby(["number_set", "target"]).agg(r=("rating", "mean"), k=("k", "first")).reset_index()
    sd = cell.groupby("number_set").agg(s=("r", "std"), k=("k", "first")).dropna()
    a = sd.loc[sd["k"] == 1, "s"]
    b = sd.loc[sd["k"] >= 3, "s"]
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(a.mean() - b.mean())

results.name: shared_decade_bonus
results.description: Among multi-example sets, yes-rate for targets whose tens digit equals some example's tens digit minus yes-rate for targets that share no example's tens digit (targets that are examples excluded); observed > null means the model under-produces endorsement driven by same-decade similarity, which it has no feature for.

results.name: partial_majority_final_digit
results.description: In sets of >=3 examples where all but one example share a final digit (not all), yes-rate for targets with that majority final digit minus yes-rate for other targets; observed > null means the model (which only reacts to a digit shared by ALL examples) under-produces endorsement of near-unanimous final-digit patterns.
